patternId: A unique slug identifying this pattern config (e.g., 'my-podcast'). Used as the folder name in the config repository.
patternDisplayName: A human-friendly name shown in the browse list. Defaults to the config ID if left empty.
podcastGuid: The podcast's globally unique identifier from its RSS feed. When set, this takes priority over feed URL matching for more reliable identification.
feedUrls: One or more RSS feed URLs that identify this podcast. The app matches incoming feeds against these URLs to determine which pattern config to apply.
yearGroupedEpisodes: When enabled, the main episode list in the app groups episodes by their publication year with year headers.
playlistId: A unique slug for this playlist within the pattern (e.g., 'season-1'). Used as the filename in the config repository.
displayName: The name shown to users in the app. Choose something descriptive like 'Seasons' or 'Story Arcs'.
resolverType: Determines how episodes are grouped into this playlist. Each resolver uses a different strategy to organize episodes.
resolverType_rss: RSS Metadata: Groups episodes by their season number from RSS feed metadata. Best for podcasts that properly tag seasons in their feed (e.g., itunes:season).
resolverType_category: Category: Groups episodes by matching their titles against regex patterns you define in the 'groups' section. Use when episodes follow naming conventions like 'Arc 1: ...' or 'Mystery Series: ...'.
resolverType_year: Year: Groups episodes by their publication year. Good for long-running podcasts where yearly grouping is a natural fit.
resolverType_titleAppearanceOrder: Title Appearance Order: Groups episodes by a recurring pattern in their titles, ordered by when each pattern first appears in the feed. Useful for podcasts with titled story arcs or series.
priority: Controls the order in which playlists claim episodes. Lower numbers are processed first and claim matching episodes, excluding them from later playlists. Playlists with filters are always processed before filter-less fallback playlists, regardless of priority.
playlistStructure: Determines how resolver results are organized. 'Split' creates separate top-level playlists for each group. 'Grouped' collects all groups inside a single parent playlist with group cards.
episodeFilters: Episode filters applied before resolver processing. Having any filter makes this a 'filtered' definition, processed before filter-less fallbacks. Require filters are ANDed (episode must match all); exclude filters reject any match.
filterTitle: A case-insensitive regex pattern matched against episode titles. Only episodes matching all require patterns and none of the exclude patterns are passed to the resolver.
showYearHeaders: When enabled, episode lists show year separator headers, helping users orient themselves in long episode lists.
showDateRange: When enabled, each group card displays the date range of its episodes (earliest to latest), giving users a quick sense of the group's timespan.
userSortable: When enabled, users can change the sort order at runtime by flipping between ascending and descending order.
prependSeasonNumber: When enabled, group titles are prefixed with the season number (e.g. S13 Regular Episodes). Groups with sortKey 0 are excluded.
nullSeasonGroupKey: Routes episodes with null or zero season numbers into this group key. For example, set to 999 to collect special episodes in a 'Season 999' group.
groupId: Unique identifier for this group within the playlist. Used as the internal key.
groupDisplayName: The name shown to users for this group in the app.
groupPattern: A regex matched against episode titles. Episodes matching this pattern are assigned to this group. Leave empty to create a catch-all group for unmatched episodes.
groupListSort: Override the default sort order for groups. Only takes effect when playlist structure is 'Grouped'. Has no effect in split mode.
sortField: The field to sort groups by. 'playlistNumber' uses the group key, 'newestEpisodeDate' uses the latest episode date, 'alphabetical' sorts by display name.
sortOrder: Ascending (A-Z, oldest first, lowest number first) or descending (Z-A, newest first, highest number first).
yearBinding: Controls how groups relate to year headers. 'None' shows a flat list. 'Pin to Year' places each group under the year of its earliest episode. 'Split by Year' shows a group once per year it contains episodes.
titleExtractor: Extracts a display name from episode data for use as group/playlist titles. Supports regex capture groups, templates, and recursive fallback chains. Not used by the Category resolver, which uses static display names from group definitions.
titleExtractorSource: The episode field to extract from: title, description, seasonNumber, or episodeNumber.
titleExtractorPattern: A regex applied to the source value. Use capture groups to extract portions of the text.
titleExtractorGroup: Which regex capture group to use (0 = full match, 1 = first group, etc.).
titleExtractorTemplate: A template string with {value} placeholder. For example, 'Season {value}' turns '1' into 'Season 1'.
titleExtractorFallbackValue: A static string returned when all extraction steps fail and the episode has no season number.
episodeExtractor: Extracts season and episode numbers from episode titles or descriptions. Supports primary and fallback patterns, nullable season extraction (episode-only mode), and RSS metadata fallback.
episodeExtractorSource: The episode field to extract from: title or description.
episodeExtractorPattern: A regex with capture groups for season and/or episode numbers.
episodeExtractorSeasonGroup: Which capture group contains the season number. Leave empty to skip season extraction (episode-only mode).
episodeExtractorEpisodeGroup: Which capture group contains the episode number (default: 2).
episodeExtractorFallbackSeason: Season number to assign when only the fallback pattern matches (e.g., 0 for special episodes).
episodeExtractorFallbackPattern: A secondary regex tried when the primary pattern doesn't match. Used for catching special/bonus episodes.
episodeExtractorFallbackCaptureGroup: Which capture group in the fallback pattern contains the episode number (default: 1).
episodeExtractorFallbackToRss: When no pattern matches, use the episode number from RSS metadata instead. Useful as a last-resort fallback.
